messages:
jordan: FYI - ACME reported a sudden burst yesterday that caused 429s and the customer says their "quota_exhausted" error popped after ~2 minutes. They ran a batch that spiked to a lot of tokens. They suspect 'burst credits' drained quickly. Any quick triage tips before I reply to them?

luis: Do we know which API route? text-generation or embeddings? Also what's their plan / tier? Short spikes should be absorbed by the burst pool unless the token/sec avg is too high for the burst window.

jordan: Text generation, streaming responses. Plan = hosted (pay-as-you-go). I pulled this from their logs: several parallel requests ~120 req/s for ~90s, avg prompt+response ~1.8k tokens. They hit 429s at 90s and then Retry-After for a couple mins.

marta: Ok — sounds like classic burst-credit exhaustion. Quick explainer to share: we allow short bursts by drawing from an account-level "burst credit" pool that refills slowly. If sustained traffic over the refill rate continues, the pool hits zero and we return 429/"quota_exhausted". The smoothing layer attempts to smooth bursts over a configurable window (defaults: 60s window, refill tuned to plan).

marta: Concrete numbers (approx): default refill ~= 1.5k tokens/sec for hosted base plans and a burst pool of ~90k tokens. A spike that consumes > burst_pool within the window will get throttled. In the example above: 120 req/s * 1800 tokens ~= 216k tokens/sec — way above refill, so pool would drop to zero quickly.

oliver: I pulled their usage graphs from the console: https://console.redwood.ai/customers/acme/usage (internal link) — shows a sharp 2-minute peak starting 2026-11-03T14:23:xxZ. Confirmed token-rate spike.

luis: For remediation and customer guidance: two approaches — server-side (us) and client-side (them). Server-side we can: 1) temporarily increase burst pool for a short window, 2) enable an account-level smoothing policy that throttles slightly earlier but avoids 429 storms, or 3) propose Dedicated or committed capacity for predictable throughput.

marta: Client-side best practices to avoid hitting pool: use a token-bucket/leaky-bucket rate limiter, add jittered exponential backoff on 429, and stagger long-running jobs. Example pseudocode (JS):

```
// simple client-side leaky bucket
const bucket = {capacity: 1000, tokens: 1000, refillRatePerSec: 50};
setInterval(() => { bucket.tokens = Math.min(bucket.capacity, bucket.tokens + bucket.refillRatePerSec); }, 1000);
async function sendRequest(reqCost) {
  while (bucket.tokens < reqCost) { await sleep(100 + Math.random()*200); }
  bucket.tokens -= reqCost;
  return client.generate(req);
}
```

marta: And handling 429s: retry with exponential backoff + jitter and honor Retry-After header. Example: 500ms * 2^attempt + random(0,200ms). If Retry-After provided, use that as a floor.

oliver: For short-term recovery we can also enable a transient burst boost (ops action) for N minutes. That is usually simplest for one-off events. I'll need approval from provisioning and billing to make it billable.

jordan: Customer asked if we can smooth on our side via an account setting. Can we flip an account-level smoothing policy to be more aggressive so they see fewer 429s (accept slightly higher latency)?

marta: Yes — we have an account flag: `smoothing.mode = conservative|balanced|aggressive`. Conservative = lower throttling threshold (avoids 429, more queueing/latency); Aggressive = higher throughput tolerance. For hosted customers we can temporarily set `smoothing.mode=conservative` for 10–30 minutes. Tradeoff: it increases P95 latency.

luis: Operational runbook to follow if customer wants immediate help:
1) Ask customer to enable client-side smoothing immediately (share code snippet).
2) Offer a temporary burst credit increase for X minutes — open internal ticket for provisioning.
3) If they expect sustained elevated traffic, recommend Dedicated or a committed uplift.

oliver: Quick commands for our internal use to confirm usage and adjust policy:
```
# get 1h token usage for account
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_ADMIN" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/internal/usage?account=acme&window=1h" | jq .tokens_per_sec

# set smoothing (ops only)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_ADMIN" -d '{"smoothing.mode":"conservative","duration_minutes":30}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/internal/accounts/acme/smoothing
```

jordan: I'll draft a concise reply for the customer with suggested quick fixes + ask if they want us to apply a temporary smoothing/credit bump. Draft below — please flag edits.

jordan: "Hi — thanks for the logs. We see a short, intense spike that consumed your account's burst credits and caused 429s. Two immediate options: (1) apply a client-side rate limiter (sample code attached) and exponential backoff to smooth retries immediately; (2) we can temporarily increase your burst allocation or apply a conservative smoothing policy on our side for 10–30 minutes to absorb the spike. Long-term: if you expect sustained high throughput, we recommend Dedicated or a committed capacity uplift to avoid throttles and unpredictable overages. Would you like us to apply a temporary smoothing/credits bump now?"

marta: Looks good — add a sentence about billing so it's explicit: "Note: temporary credit bumps are billable and will appear as overage unless moved to committed capacity."

oliver: I'll create the provisioning request. Also linking internal ticket SUP-8342 for the bump.

deploy-bot: Ticket SUP-8342 created and assigned to oliver. :gear:

luis: Action items — jordan: send reply to customer w/ client code + link to docs (https://docs.redwood.ai/rate-limits#burst-credits). oliver: attach graphs and create provisioning ticket (SUP-8342). marta: ready to flip smoothing flag if customer agrees.

jordan: Will send combined reply in ~30m with the options and the JS snippet. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

luis: FYI we should add a short KB for common burst patterns + example backoff configs so support can paste quicker next time. I'll start a draft.

marta: +1. Good case study.

oliver: Done here — leaving comments in SUP-8342 with recommended duration 20 minutes and cost estimate.

jordan: Closing loop — customer replied and asked us to apply smoothing for 20 minutes while they roll out client-side limiter. I requested the transient bump in SUP-8342.

luis: perfect. monitoring watch set for the window.

marta: closing thread once bump completes and we verify no further 429s.
